sampled_function.v33_error: v33 sampled e = k_i + s_i (diagonal pairing) and dropped c entirely
sampled_function.challenge_cell_disclosure: fixture challenge is a full-width scalar mod m=2^38; production's is uniform mod r=2^255 -- the MULTIPLIER IS PRESENT in both, its width is fixture-regime
sampled_function.key: low w bits of key_mixed_final(canonical-even phi(e)), shipped 168-bit kernel
sampled_function.surrogate: DISCLOSED: phi = SHAKE(e) mod p stands in for y([e]P); dependence structure exact (Cartesian product, shared challenge, shared walk list, canonical-even, full kernel), curve group law not executed

The 168-bit production envelope is NOT an extrapolation of these rows: it is the birthday arithmetic kappa*N^2/2^169 over the 168-bit image, whose premise (every stored bit is a function of all six limbs) is the measured-avalanche property in key_collision_test.py / key-collision-v32.json.
charged_kappa_rule: max upper95 over POWERED cells (expected cross pairs >= 100), with the 1.231 carried envelope as a floor; the low-power diagonal control is reported and does not set the charge

hist_regression_control.verdict: the audit check `hist_side_count_matches_expectation` FIRES on the planted v33 histogram and passes on the both-side histogram

v33_delta.cause: v33 paired k_i+s_i (diagonal) and withheld the challenge; the diagonal cell is retained here and reproduces the elevation, which is why the pairing was the defect and not the kernel

verdict_flaw_1_2: census samples the Cartesian base-by-walk product with the challenge multiplier inside phi, histograms the A-union-B stream it divides by, reports per-pool kappa with a cluster bootstrap, and prices key width as a measured 4-rung ladder with an explicitly non-extrapolated scope
